questions.text:
Direction: In each of the following questions, there are three statements which is followed by two conclusions. Choose the conclusions which logically follow from the given statements.

Statements:

No Belt is Bag.

Some Purse are Wallet.

Some wallet are Belt.

Conclusions:

I. Some Purse are Bag.

II. No Bag is Purse.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follow
Neither conclusion I or II follow

questions.explanation:
The least possible Venn diagram is shown below

Conclusions:

I. Some Purse are Bag → False (It is possible but not definite. As no direct relation between Bag and Purse is given).

So it is considered as Cannot be determined.
II. No Bag is Purse → False (It is possible but not definite. As no direct relation between Bag and Purse is given).

Part of Bag can go in Purse.

So, it is considered as Cannot be determined.

Thus conclusion I and II form a complementary pair.

Hence, Either conclusion I or II follow.

Additional Information:

Conditions for the Either Or:

1. Both the conclusion must be Cannot be determined.

2. Both the objects in both the conclusion must be same.

3. If one conclusion is positive, then other should be negative.

Complementary pairs:

1. All - Some not (Positions of the object should be same in the conclusion)

2. Some - No

questions.explanation:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows

Conclusions:

I. Some D being A is a possibility. → True (The possibility is true, and D can be part of A).

Additional Information

1. Some X are Y means some part of the X circle is within the Y circle.

3. All X is Y means the whole circle X lies within the Y circle.

4. If there is no exact conclusion for the given statements then the possibility case arises.

5. If Only X is Y means all Y is X, and Y cannot make Positive relation with any other element except X negative can be possible.

You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Statements: 

All White are Skies.

All Skies are Moons.

No Moon is Earth.

Conclusions:

I. Some Moons are White.

II. No Sky is Earth.

III. Some Earth are White.
questions.explanation:
The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows

Conclusions:

I. Some Moons are White → True (All White are Skies and All Skies are Moons then Some Moons are White, possible to be definite. So, it is true).

II. No Sky is Earth → True (All Skies are Moons and No Moons is Earth so No Sky is Earth, possible to be definite. So, it is true).

III. Some Earth are White → False (No Moon is Earth and All White are Moons so Some Earth is White, not possible to be definite. So, it is false).

Hence, Both I and II follow.
